Returns '%s' if value is None or starts with '\\x', otherwise returns the result of get_encrypt_sql(connection).
Returns a DecryptedCol for the given alias unless the alias matches the model’s table and the output field is the instance itself, in which case it returns the cached column.
Returns an encrypted SQL placeholder using the public PGP key from settings.
Detects duplicate keys in a YAML document and records the line numbers where each duplicate occurs.
Computes linear regression parameters (slope, intercept) and their chi‑square, Hessian, and covariance from the data in Q, optionally using a supplied slope.
Computes the inverse covariance matrix by recursing over the full matrix and returns the result stored in the tree root.
Recursively computes and stores inverse covariance matrices and related vectors for each nonterminal node in a tree, optionally constructing full matrices based on child nodes and branch variances.
Calculates node‐specific average statistics (Q and O matrices) for a phylogenetic tree by propagating tip and branch values through postorder and preorder traversals.

Propagates node‐level average statistics, computing updated moments (means, variances, covariances, etc.) based on whether the node is terminal or internal, handling outgroup cases and special variance conditions.
Calculates the correlation coefficient between tip values and node values in the tree, returning the explained variance.
Calculates averages, builds a base regression model using the tree root’s Q and an optional slope, assigns the explained variance to the model’s 'r_val', and returns the model.
Finds the optimal root position on a tree by evaluating chi‑square across branches, performing regression, and computing the Hessian and covariance for the best root.
Sets the temperature interpolation function Tc from given values or a constant, handling mismatched lengths with a warning, and then updates the merger rate integral.
Calculates a time‑dependent branch count for a phylogenetic tree by aggregating node events, summing changes at each time point, and building a linear interpolation of the resulting branch counts.
Calculates the cost of a branch by subtracting the integral merger rates over the branch and adding a log‑weighted term of the total merger rate scaled by the given multiplicity.
Sets the merger cost on each clade’s branch length interpolator to the object’s cost for all non‑root clades in the tree.
Optimizes the coalescent time scale Tc by minimizing the negative total likelihood within bounds, updating Tc on success or reverting to the initial value on failure.
Samples a sequence from a profile matrix (optionally normalizing and sampling or taking the most likely state) and returns the sequence, the profile values at the chosen states, and the indices.

Normalizes each row of a profile array to sum to one, optionally applying a log‑sum‑exp transformation for numerical stability, and returns the normalized array along with the log of the scaling factor.
Sets a GTR or GTR_site_specific object to the instance after validating its type.
Sets the GTR model for the TreeAnc instance, accepting a string or GTR object, configuring logging, and raising an error for invalid types.
Sets the sequence length if it hasn't been set yet; otherwise logs an error if an attempt is made to reset it.
Assigns sequences to tree nodes from an alignment, handling missing data and logging warnings, extends the profile, and returns a reduced alignment.
Initializes the tree by setting the root’s branch and mutation lengths, clearing its mutations, ladderizing the tree, preparing internal nodes, and building a lookup dictionary of leaf nodes by name.
Initializes node attributes, assigns names to internal nodes, propagates bad_branch flags up the tree, calculates distances to the root, and updates the internal node count.
Calculates and assigns the distance from the root to each node in the tree.
Reconstructs ancestral sequences using ML or Fitch methods (optionally inferring GTR) and returns the result.
Computes a normalized mutation probability matrix for a branch (using the node’s marginal profile and the GTR model), optionally expanding it to the full sequence.
Returns a reduced sequence from node.cseq based on a mapping, optionally including additional constant sites.

Reconstructs ancestral states with the Fitch algorithm, assigns sequences and profiles to all tree nodes (resolving ambiguities at the root), counts differences from parent sequences, and returns that count.
Computes the Fitch intersection of character states at a given position across a node’s clades, and if the intersection is empty, concatenates all the states instead.
Computes the intersection of multiple arrays by iteratively intersecting pairs until a single common element list remains.
Returns the likelihood sequence for a specified position (or the total sequence) after ensuring marginal ancestral inference has run, optionally mapping full to reduced positions.

Computes the log‑likelihood of each character across a phylogenetic tree by iterating over nodes postorder, applying the substitution model’s transition probabilities and base frequencies to accumulate log probabilities for ancestral sequences.
Returns the greater of a minimum branch length (scaled by one_mutation) and the node’s mutation length if use_mutation_length is true, otherwise the node’s branch length.
Optimizes branch lengths of a phylogenetic tree (jointly or marginally), updating node lengths, optionally storing old lengths, logging progress, and warning if long branches are detected.

Optimizes all branch lengths of a phylogenetic tree globally by minimizing the negative log‑likelihood with a gradient‑based optimizer, then updates node lengths, mutation lengths, and tree parameters accordingly.
Computes and returns the optimal branch length for a node, using compressed sequence data if present or otherwise calculating it from the parent and node sequences.

Iteratively optimizes ancestral sequences and branch lengths, optionally reusing branch lengths, pruning short branches, and updating likelihoods until convergence or a maximum number of iterations is reached.
Returns a MultipleSeqAlignment of all tree nodes, reconstructing ancestral sequences if not already present.
Computes a 3‑D array from Pi and W, then for each slice sets its diagonal to the negative of the sum over the first axis.
Creates an instance of the class with the supplied kwargs, assigns rates using the provided mu, pi, and W values, and returns the configured instance.
Returns an instance of a nucleotide or amino acid substitution model based on the provided model name, raising an error if the name is not recognized.

Normalizes the stationary distribution, breaks degeneracy in the rate matrix, rescales the rate matrix and mutation rate, and verifies that the diagonal of the GTR rate matrix sums to zero, raising an error if not.
Computes the (log) probability of a compressed sequence pair at time t using the expQt matrix, handling zero entries, and returns either the log probability or its exponentiated value.
Computes the optimal t for two sequences by compressing them and delegating to optimal_t_compressed.

Finds the optimal branch length between two sequences by minimizing the negative log‑probability (using compressed or profile models), falling back to a Hamming‑distance estimate if the optimization fails.
Computes the (log) probability of observing a pair of profile sequences at time t, optionally ignoring gaps, by applying a transition matrix and weighting by multiplicity.
Computes the time‑evolved profile by multiplying the input profile with the transposed matrix exponential of Q at time t, optionally returning the logarithm of the result.
Computes the weighted log‑likelihood of a sequence under the model’s initial state distribution.
Sets the branch length mode to 'joint', 'marginal', or 'input', or infers it from the tree’s maximum branch length if not explicitly provided.

Filters outlier tree nodes by computing clock residuals, marking branches with residuals beyond a multiple of the inter‑quartile range, optionally reroots the tree, and can plot the updated root‑to‑tip distances.
Plots a root‑to‑tip regression of the tree, optionally adding internal nodes and confidence intervals.
Resolves polytomies in the tree by collapsing single‑child nodes and adding new nodes as needed, returning the number of new nodes introduced.
Prints the tree log‑likelihood components (sequence, tree, coalescent) for joint or marginal inference, handling errors if inference has not been run.
Adds a coalescent prior to the tree, configuring and optimizing the coalescent model based on the specified Tc value, then attaches it to the tree.
Finds the optimal root position for a phylogenetic tree by running a regression on branch lengths and returns the node that maximizes the fit.
Ensures a phylogenetic tree exists by inferring one if missing, cleaning the temporary directory, loading the tree, and returning 0 on success or 1 on failure.
Creates a GTR model from the given parameters, parsing custom settings or falling back to a default Jukes‑Cantor model, and returns the resulting model.
Reads a VCF alignment file, extracts the sequences and reference, optionally infers fixed base frequencies, and returns the alignment, reference, and fixed_pi.
Reconstructs ancestral sequences from a VCF/alignment using a GTR model, outputs the inferred tree and sequences, and returns a success status.
Calculates the full width at half maximum (FWHM) of a distribution given as an interpolation or Distribution object.
Creates a delta‑function distribution at a given position with an optional weight and minimum width.
Multiplies a list of Distribution objects, handling delta functions and overlapping support, and returns the resulting distribution.
Assigns date constraints to each node in the tree, marking branches as bad when dates are missing or invalid, and aborts with an error if too many terminal branches lack valid dates.
Sets up and returns a TreeRegression object configured with tip and branch values and variances, optionally incorporating covariation and confidence settings.
Creates a time‑calibrated phylogenetic tree using maximum likelihood, optionally applying marginal or joint date optimization, and then converts the dates.
Computes the log‑likelihood of a time tree by summing branch‑length contributions for all nodes and adding the root sequence likelihood if an alignment is present.
Converts each node’s time in a tree to a human‑readable date string, logs warnings for nodes dated after the present, and assigns the formatted date to the node.
Calculates date uncertainty bounds from a node’s rate variation using a specified confidence interval, returning an array of adjusted dates or None if no variation data is available.
Computes a posterior probability region containing a specified fraction of mass for a node, handling delta, left/right/center peaks, and returns a combined confidence interval.
Returns the x‑value at which the interpolation object reaches its minimum, raising an error if the minimum cannot be determined.
Computes the median of an interpolated distribution by evaluating a weighted cumulative sum over a finely‑sampled grid and returning the grid point where the cumulative weight reaches half the total.
Returns a numeric representation of a date as the year plus the fractional part of the year based on the day of year, or None if an error occurs.
Creates a new instance from a regression model dictionary, initializing clock_rate, intercept, chisq, valid_confidence, covariance, and r_val attributes.
Establishes and returns a socket connection to the guacd server, creating it if it does not already exist.
Closes the client connection, clears the client reference, marks the connection as closed, and logs the closure.
Receives a complete instruction from the client by buffering incoming data until the instruction terminator is found, then returns the decoded line or closes the connection if no data is received.
Sends data to the client after logging it.
Logs a debug message and sends the instruction encoded as bytes.
Performs a Guacamole handshake by selecting the protocol, exchanging size/audio/video/image capabilities, sending connection arguments, and receiving a ready response with a client ID.
Encodes a Unicode string to UTF‑8 on Python 2, otherwise returns the string unchanged.
Loads an instance from an instruction string, validating its termination and decoding its arguments.
Encodes an argument to UTF‑8 and returns a string of the form "<length><ELEM_SEP><utf8 bytes>".
Encodes an instruction by concatenating its opcode and arguments, separating them with ARG_SEP and terminating with INST_TERM.
Returns the API URL path for the class, including its resource version and API-formatted name.
Returns the full URL for the instance by appending its ID to the class URL, or raises an exception if the ID is missing.
Returns the API URL path for the class, including its resource version and API name.
Downloads a file from a URL, saving it to a given path or a temporary location, and returns the file path.
Retrieves the parent object of the current job by looking up the parent class from the job model and calling its retrieve method with the parent job ID.
Prompts the user for a SolveBio domain, checks if it supports password login, then asks for email and password and returns them, or exits with an SSO message if password login is not supported.
Prompts the user for domain, email, and password, authenticates with the SolveBio API, and sets the client token if successful.
Prints the current user if logged in, otherwise prints a not‑logged‑in message.
Prints a login confirmation message showing the user’s email, domain, and role.
Creates a clone of the object with the given positional filters, optionally adding a Filter built from keyword arguments.
Creates a clone of the object with a genomic range filter applied.
Creates a clone of the object filtered to a specific chromosome and position, optionally requiring an exact match.
Combines positional and keyword arguments into a facets dictionary, validates the keys, executes a faceted query with no limit, and returns the facets from the response.
Recursively processes a list of filter objects and dictionaries, flattening nested filter structures into a single list of filter dictionaries.
Iterates over a paginated data source, fetching new pages as needed and returning the next item.
Executes a paginated query, builds parameters, logs the request, sends it via the client, handles SolveError, logs response timing, and returns the query parameters and response.
Creates a dataset migration from the current dataset to a target dataset, optionally following the migration until completion.
Parses command‑line arguments, sets the SolveBio API host and key (falling back to local credentials if needed), updates the client configuration, and runs the chosen function.
Downloads all files and subfolders from a specified remote vault path to a local directory, optionally forcing overwrite and supporting a dry‑run mode.
Creates a new instance of the class using the ID from the provided values, refreshes it with those values, and returns the instance.
Logs out a user by revoking the OAuth token (if present), clearing cookies, and redirecting to the home page.
Sends an HTTP request with the given method and URL, handling auth, headers, JSON or file data, retrying on rate limits, and returns either the raw response or parsed JSON.
Retrieves a child object of the specified task type using its ID and client.
Cancels the object by setting its status to "canceled", attempts to save, and restores the original status if the save fails.

Parses the VCF INFO dictionary’s ANN field, converting each annotation string into a structured dictionary (splitting on ‘|’, mapping to fields, handling empty values, and splitting annotations on ‘&’) and returns the updated INFO.
Converts a VCF row into a dictionary containing genomic coordinates, a SolveBio variant ID, allele details, and parsed INFO fields.
Retrieves the password for the API host from the user's .netrc file, returning None if no credentials are found.
Saves the hosts and macros configuration to a file at the given path.
Formats a value into a string based on its type, returning a default for None, converting ints, binary/text types, and floats with a specified format, and otherwise converting the value to a string.
Normalizes various tabular data structures (dicts, pandas DataFrames, etc.) into a list of rows and headers, handling header extraction, optional sorting, and padding missing headers.
Builds a formatted table row string from cells with padding, separators, and optional truncation to fit within the terminal width.
Builds a table line using the given column widths, padding, and fill character, then returns the formatted row string.
Creates a list of cell strings prefixed with alignment attributes based on the given column alignments.
Formats a table into a string using the given format, headers, rows, column widths, and alignments, adding optional header, separator, and padding lines.
Migrates the current dataset to a target dataset (by ID or Dataset object), optionally following the migration process.
Validates and normalizes a vault resource path, extracting domain, vault, and object path components, handling overrides, and returning the cleaned full path and a dictionary of parsed parts.
Uploads local files or directories to a specified remote vault path, validating the vault and remote path, and recursively uploading folders or individual files.
Validates and normalizes a vault path string, handling defaults and the special "~" case, and returns the full path and its parsed components.
Validates that a given API host URL is non‑empty, has an HTTP or HTTPS scheme, and contains a network location, raising a SolveError if any check fails.
Adds URLs, files, directories, or glob patterns to the manifest by delegating to add_url or add_file, raising an error for invalid paths.
Yields annotated results for records in chunks, updating annotator parameters with any provided kwargs.
Sends the given data, expression, and options to the '/v1/evaluate' endpoint and returns the server’s result.
Sets the object's format name if it is supported; otherwise raises a ValueError.
Registers a new output formatter by adding an OutputFormatHandler instance to the class's `_output_formats` dictionary.
Formats data and headers into a specified output format, applying optional preprocessors and inferring column types if needed.
Creates an iterator of tabulated rows from data and headers, applying optional formatting and whitespace preservation.
Returns the path to the user's configuration directory for the given app, handling Windows, macOS, and Linux XDG conventions.
Returns a list of system configuration directories for the given app, selecting appropriate paths based on the operating system and XDG settings.
Loads and validates the default configuration file, raising errors on validation failures, and updates the current configuration with the defaults.
Reads configuration files, optionally loading a default config first.
Returns the full path to the user’s configuration file by joining the user config directory (derived from the app name and author) with the filename.
Returns a list of system configuration file paths by joining each directory from get_system_config_dirs(self.app_name, self.app_author) with self.filename.
Returns a list of full file paths by joining each directory in self.additional_dirs with self.filename.
Writes the default configuration to the user’s config file, unless overwrite is False and the file already exists.
Reads a list of config files, updates the object with each file’s configuration, and returns a dictionary of any validation errors or True if all files are valid.
Truncates a string to a specified maximum width if it exceeds that width.
Applies a series of string replacements to the input string and returns the modified string.
Executes a list of commands sequentially, exiting with an error if any command returns 1.
Applies default and supplied command options to a command string, updating it with each option’s effect and returning the modified command.
Replaces placeholders of the form {{option:…}} in a command string with the captured option value if active, otherwise removes the placeholder.
Initializes options by setting the default branch to 'master', the fix flag to False, and then calling the superclass's initialize_options method.
Runs pep8radius on the current branch with optional in‑place fix and verbose output, then exits.
Runs a sequence of documentation commands: clean, generate HTML, and view.
Truncates every string in the data rows and headers to a specified maximum width, returning a generator of truncated rows and a list of truncated headers.
Formats numeric fields in a dataset according to specified integer and float formats based on column types, returning the formatted data and headers.
Formats a row by pairing each header with its corresponding field, joining them with ' | ' and returning the result as a newline‑separated string.
Filters the separator options from kwargs and forwards them with data and headers to vertical_table.
Yields each row of a formatted table built from the given headers and data, using the specified table format and optional title.
Renders a template file by replacing {{key}} placeholders with provided keyword arguments and writes the result to a destination file.
Checks whether the given attribute type is one of the numeric PKCS#11 constants and returns True if it is, otherwise False.
Checks if the given attribute type is one of the predefined boolean attribute constants.
Checks if a type is binary by ensuring it is not a boolean, string, or numeric type.
Generates a cryptographic key using the provided template and mechanism, returning the key handle.
Generates a public/private key pair using the given templates and mechanism, returning the handles for the new keys.
Finds and returns a list of object handles that match the given PKCS#11 template.

Inserts an optional icon into a QR code image, loading it from a file, URL, or static directory, resizing it to fit within a fraction of the QR code, and pasting it at the center or a specified position.
Exports specified gene panels (optionally in BED format and for a given version) to stdout, aborting if no panels are provided.
Finds the first date on or after d that matches the specified weekday.
Counts occurrences of a recurring event within a month, optionally starting on a given day, iterating by a step interval and respecting end dates and an optional end‑on day.
Counts each day from the start date down to the end date, calling `self.count_it(day)` for valid dates that are not past `self.end_repeat`, while ignoring invalid dates.
Sets the number of days to 14, calculates biweekly repeats, adjusts for chunk events, and appends the resulting dates to the count dictionary.
Handles a single chunk event by generating its occurrences for the current month and updating the event count dictionary.
Yields variants for a given document or case, retrieving them from the adapter, sorting by chromosome and position, and returning each variant object.
Exports verified variant data into a list of rows, each row containing variant metadata, sample details, genotype and allele depth information, and caller-specific fields.
Creates a list of rows containing variant position, change, combined string, protein effects, gene symbols, and allele depths for the specified sample.
Updates a user’s roles and institute memberships by adding or removing specified roles and institutes, logging each change, and then persisting the updated user record.
Retrieves and returns STR variant data for a given institute and case, applying filters and pagination.
Calls the sv_variant controller with the given institute ID, case name, and variant ID, returning the result.
Calls the controllers.str_variant function with the given institute_id, case_name, and variant_id and returns its result.
Verifies a variant for a specified institute and case by invoking the variant verification controller, handling user comments, and flashing an error if no verification recipients are configured.
Handles GET requests to export ClinVar data and POST requests to create or update a ClinVar submission from form data, then redirects to the submissions page.
Retrieves cancer variant data for a given institute and case by delegating to the controller and returns the result.
Handles GET requests to retrieve ACMG variant data and POST requests to submit new criteria, then flashes a classification message and redirects to the variant page.
Handles retrieving an evaluation, deleting it on POST requests, and returns its details along with related institute, case, variant, and ACMG criteria.
Retrieves a list of criteria from the request, passes them to get_acmg, and returns the resulting classification as JSON.
Handles uploading a gene symbol file, updates the symbol set, and redirects to the appropriate variants page.

Downloads verified variant Excel files for the current user’s institutes, zips them into a temporary archive, serves the ZIP to the client, and cleans up the temp files (or flashes a warning if none were found).
Creates a mapping from each gene alias to its true HGNC ID and a set of all HGNC IDs that share that alias.
Adds an 'incomplete_penetrance' flag to each gene in the genes dictionary that is identified from HPO lines.
Links gene data from HGNC, Ensembl, ExAC, OMIM, and HPO to build a comprehensive gene dictionary.
Sends an authenticated HTTP request to a matchmaker server, logs the request and response, and returns the JSON response (including status code) or an error message.
Retrieves a list of connected nodes from the Matchmaker service using the provided base URL and token.
Returns the cytoband data for a given chromosome and position from the CYTOBANDS dictionary.
Determines a subcategory string based on the category and length comparison, returning 'snv' or 'indel' for SNV/indel/cancer types, or the svtype for structural variants.
Calculates the length of a genetic variant from its type, reference/alternate lengths, coordinates, and optional SV details.
Computes the end coordinate of a genetic variant based on its type (SNV, indel, cancer, SV, BND) and optional SV fields.
Parses a variant object to compute its genomic position, end, length, subcategory, mate ID, cytoband coordinates, and end chromosome, then returns these details in a dictionary.
Parses a cytoband file and demonstrates querying intervals by chromosome and position.
Handles uploading a CSV to create or update gene panels and returns panel and institute data for display.
Updates a panel with a new version from the form and redirects to its page.
Exports a panel as a PDF report by rendering a template with panel data and returning the generated PDF.

Handles adding or editing a gene in a panel by populating a form with transcript options, processing submissions to add or update gene data, and returning the panel, form, gene, and panel_gene context.
Saves a delivery report to a case, logging success or aborting on error.
Retrieves a list of HPO terms from the store, optionally filtered by a query and limited in number, and returns them in a dictionary under the key 'phenotypes'.
Logs a message, retrieves the adapter, and prints the _id of each document in the whitelist collection.
Retrieves an HPO term by ID, builds a phenotype dictionary, and returns the original term.
Retrieves and compiles HGNC gene data for the specified ID across genome builds, adding positions, links, phenotypes, and metadata into a structured dictionary.

Returns a sorted list of Event objects for a specific day, based on event counts and start times.
Retrieves a paginated list of structural variants for a case, parsing each variant and indicating whether additional pages of results are available.
Returns STR variants by delegating to the generic variants function.

Retrieves institute, case, and variant data, populates variant details (callers and comments), and returns a dictionary containing the institute, case, variant, overlapping SNVs, and ranking/dismissal options.

Retrieves a structural variant, enriches it with institute and case data, frequencies, callers, overlapping SNVs, gene links, comments, and ClinVar significance, then returns a dictionary containing the variant and related information.

Updates a variant object by adding missing compound data, sorting compounds, correcting gene symbols, adding predictions and comments, normalizing ACMG codes and length, and optionally persisting changes.
Creates a header list for variant export by appending sample‑specific AD reference, AD alternate, and GT quality fields to a base header.

Collects canonical transcript information for each gene, formatting it as a string (including gene ID if multiple genes) and returns a dictionary with a list of these strings under the key 'canonical_transcripts'.

Creates a formatted string summarizing a transcript’s refseq ID, gene part type (exon, intron, or intergenic), part count, coding sequence name, and protein sequence name, optionally prefixed by a given gene name.

Determines if a variant is common, uncommon, or rare based on the highest frequency from thousand_genomes or exac data.
Yields each clnsig entry with a human‑readable description (mapping numeric codes via CLINSIG_MAP when present) and a ClinVar URL based on the accession.

Exports all genes for a specified build, printing them as JSON if requested or as a tab‑delimited table with chromosome, start, end, HGNC ID, and symbol.
Builds a validated individual dictionary from input, mapping sex and phenotype codes, checking analysis type, and including optional attributes.

Determines a genetic variant’s ACMG classification (pathogenic, likely pathogenic, benign, likely benign, or uncertain significance) based on the provided ACMG evidence terms.
Adds HGNC gene and transcript data, including disease associations and panel‑specific annotations, to a variant object.

Retrieves a variant by ID (optionally within a case), enriches it with gene panel information, flags pseudoautosomal regions for X/Y chromosomes, and returns the variant object.
Retrieves a sorted list of gene variants from the database based on query parameters, with optional pagination.
Retrieves validation events for a given institute, enriches each variant with its case’s display name and individuals, and returns the list of these enriched variants.
Returns a list of causatives for a given case or, if no case is specified, all unique causatives linked to the specified institute.

Extracts variants from a specified VCF file for a given region or gene and writes them to a temporary file, returning the file path.
Retrieves variants for a given sample by filtering the variant collection for specified IDs, category, and non‑wild‑type genotype calls.
Creates and returns a MongoDB client connection using the supplied host, port, credentials or URI, with logging and timeout handling.
Creates a list of submission objects from form data for each variant, populating fields and generating unique IDs based on the object type.
Creates a header dictionary for a ClinVar submission CSV by selecting the appropriate base header (variant or case data) and including only fields that appear in the provided submission objects.

Loads Ensembl transcripts into the adapter, mapping them to genes, assigning HGNC IDs, selecting primary RefSeq identifiers, building transcript objects, and bulk inserting them.

Deletes a specified case (by ID or display name and institute) and removes its associated clinical and research variants, aborting if the case is not found.
Prints a tab‑separated list of individuals for a specified case or all cases matching an institute and causatives, showing case ID, individual ID, display name, sex, phenotype, mother, and father.
Parses raw MatchMaker match objects for a patient, extracting match IDs, dates, types, and associated patient scores, then returns a sorted list of parsed match dictionaries.
Lists cases for a given institute or case ID, optionally showing clinical and research variant counts and filtering out cases with fewer variants than a specified threshold.
Loads a user by email from the store, wraps it in a LoginUser instance, and returns that instance (or None if the user is not found).
Handles user login by optionally initiating Google OAuth, validating a whitelisted email, and performing login or redirecting to the public index.
Creates an Institute object with the given parameters, removes any attributes that are None, and returns the object.
Deletes an event from the event collection by its ID, converting the ID to an ObjectId if needed, and logs the deletion.
Creates an event dictionary from the given parameters, inserts it into the event collection, and returns the event.
Retrieves events from the event collection filtered by institute, case, variant, panel, and comment status, then returns them sorted by creation date descending.
Returns events from the event collection filtered by the user’s ID if a user object is supplied, otherwise returns all events.
Adds phenotype terms to a case from an HPO or OMIM term, updates the case record (and phenotype groups if requested), and logs an event for each new term.
Removes an HPO phenotype term (and optionally its group) from a case, updates the database, logs the action, and records an event.
Creates a comment event for a case or variant, validating the comment level, logging the action, and returning the created event.
Parses each individual’s genotype for a given variant by looking up their position and calling parse_genotype, returning a list of the parsed genotypes.
Checks if a given chromosome and position fall within the specified start and end coordinates, returning True only when the chromosome matches and the position is within bounds.
Handles GET requests to fetch HPO terms with a default limit, or POST requests to search for a specific HPO term and return the results along with the query and limit.
Exports transcript data from the adapter, printing a header and each transcript’s chromosome, start, end, Ensembl transcript ID, RefSeq ID, and HGNC ID.
Drops any existing exons for the given build, loads new Ensembl exons, updates the adapter indexes, and logs the time taken.
Loads a genomic region for a specified case and gene using the adapter from the context.

Parses a requirements file, recursively handling nested `-r` includes, and returns a list of requirement strings.
Returns the gene dictionary from panel_obj['genes'] that matches the given hgnc_id, or None if not found.
Updates a gene panel by parsing CSV lines, optionally replacing existing genes, and queues add/edit/delete actions for each gene.
Creates a new gene panel for a given institute from a CSV gene list, validating institute and panel uniqueness, parsing genes, building panel data, and storing it.
Updates a panel object's institute and name_and_version fields and returns it in a dict.

Retrieves gene aliases for a specified build (and optional symbol) and prints a table of each alias, its true HGNC ID, and all associated HGNC IDs.
Builds a panel dictionary from input data, validating required fields, ensuring the institute exists, creating gene objects, and raising errors if any required data is missing or genes are invalid.
Exports verified variants for a collaborator to an Excel file (or returns a success count in test mode) and logs the result.

Starts a web server (with optional livereload) after verifying MongoDB connectivity and loading the specified configuration.
Generates an MD5 hash of the space‑separated string arguments, raising a SyntaxError if any argument is not a string.
Initializes the application by reading MongoDB configuration from the app, logging the connection details, and setting up the database using the provided configuration.
Initializes the instance’s database collection attributes from the provided database object.
Logs a message and either updates or loads indexes via the adapter based on the update flag.
Sets up the scout database by ensuring an OMIM API key is available, using context defaults for institute, user, and mail, and then calling setup_scout with the adapter and these parameters.
Sets up a demo scout environment using context data and logs the database setup.
Sets up context with user and institute info, and if demo mode, configures and connects to a MongoDB database, tests the connection, and stores a MongoAdapter in the context.
Lists institutes (by ID or all) in tabular or JSON format, aborting if none are found.
Extracts and returns a list of genetic models for a given case ID from a comma‑separated string of family info.
Lists gene panels for a given institute, printing each panel’s name, version, number of genes, and date.
Adds a new institute to the database, checking for duplicate internal_id, inserting the record, and logging the operation.
Updates an institute’s database record with optional changes to sanger recipients, cutoffs, display name, phenotype groups, and logs each modification.
Fetches an institute by ID from the collection, logging the attempt and returning the result (or None if not found).
Checks whether a string matches a YYYY‑MM‑DD (or similar) date format and returns True if it does, otherwise False.
Parses a date string into a datetime object using an optional format or by splitting on common separators, defaulting to the current time if no date is provided.
Exports gene IDs and their counts for the specified HPO terms to the console.
Parses a comma‑separated list of case IDs and scores, returning the score for the specified case ID as a float, or None if not found.

Creates a new user with the given name, email, and institute memberships (optionally marking them as admin) and adds them to the adapter, aborting if any institute is missing or the add operation fails.
Checks if a MongoDB server is reachable by attempting a connection with the given host, port, and optional credentials, returning True on success and False on failure.
Initializes a MongoDB client for a Flask app using configuration values and stores the client and database in the app config.
Loads a delivery report into a MongoDB case, inserting it if missing or updating it if allowed, and raises errors for missing cases or existing reports without update.
Adds a user to the database, setting a default _id if missing, and raises an IntegrityError if the user already exists.
Handles a pileup view request by collecting alignment files, optional VCF, genome and exon data, and rendering the pileup template with the specified genomic region.

Loads exon records from the given input, filters them by Ensembl gene and transcript IDs, builds exon objects for the specified genome build, inserts them into the adapter, and logs the total and loaded counts.
Updates the compounds for a given case, aborting if the case is missing or an error occurs.

Retrieves an open ClinVar submission for a given user and institute, creating a new one if none exists.
Updates a ClinVar submission record with a new ClinVar ID and timestamp, upserting if necessary, and returns the updated document.

Handles an API request to retrieve genes based on a query parameter and returns the results as JSON.

Checks that all default panels are included in the provided panels list and that each panel exists in the database, logging warnings for missing ones, and returns a boolean indicating whether all panels are valid.
Loads clinical and research variants for a specified case and genomic region (determined by gene ID or coordinates) and logs the loading process.
Loads a case after verifying required gene panels exist, raising an error if any are missing.
Creates a decorator that renders a specified or inferred template using the wrapped function’s return value as the context.
Retrieves an institute (and optionally a case) from the store, verifies they exist, checks the current user’s access rights, and returns the objects or aborts with a 404/403 error.
Returns a list of institutes accessible to the user: all institutes if the user is an admin, otherwise only the institutes associated with the user.
Retrieves the HGNC ID for a gene, using the ID in gene_info if present or querying the adapter by symbol and matching case‑insensitively to return the true ID.
Updates a gene panel to a new version and date after verifying the panel exists and parsing the update date.

Lists all users from the adapter, printing each user’s name, email, roles, and institutes, or aborts if no users are found.
Builds an HgncGene object from a gene_info dictionary, validating required fields, setting optional attributes, and attaching phenotype objects.
Builds a panel object from parsed data and adds it to the gene panel.

Returns a set of gene symbols from all panels referenced in the given case object.

Loads and updates database indexes by dropping any existing indexes for each collection and creating the new ones defined in INDEXES.

Creates a dictionary containing the 'value', 'accession', and 'revstat' fields from the input clnsig_info.

Inserts a bulk of exon objects into the exon collection, raising an IntegrityError on duplicate key or bulk write errors.
Fetches an HGNC gene by ID or symbol (optionally for a specific genome build) and attaches its transcripts to the returned gene object.

Sends a VCF2Cytosure file as an attachment to the client, logging the file name and directory.
Returns the MultiQC report file for a given institute and case, aborting with a 404 error if the report is missing.

Retrieves the display name and vcf2cytosure value for a specific individual in a given case.

Retrieves MatchMaker matches for each patient in a case, handling errors and returning a structured result.

Updates gene, transcript, and exon data for the specified genome build(s) by fetching OMIM, HGNC, ExAC, Ensembl, and HPO information, dropping existing entries, loading the new data, and updating database indexes.

Builds an HgncTranscript object from transcript_info, validating required fields and removing None values.
Creates an institute object from the given parameters and stores it in the database via the adapter.

Assigns a user to a case by creating an event and adding the user to the case's assignees list.
Adds a new collaborator to a case, logs the share event, and updates the case document.
Adds or removes an OMIM ID from a case’s phenotype or gene diagnosis list and logs the update.
Updates a case’s analysis_checked flag (and logs the change), creates a check event, and returns the updated case.

Marks a variant as causative in a case, updates the case status to solved, logs the action, and creates corresponding case and variant events.

Updates a variant’s ACMG classification (setting or unsetting it), logs the change, records an event, and returns the updated variant.

Generates an MD5 hash key from chromosome, position, reference allele, alternate allele, variant type, and case ID.
Converts a gene panel into a tab‑separated table of HGNC fields, printing a header and rows for each gene that has an HGNC ID.
Generates a new variant ID by parsing the variant object's chromosome, position, reference, alternative, and type along with the family ID.
Returns the number of cases in the collection, optionally filtered by a given institute ID.
Updates a case’s dynamic gene panel by retrieving genes via HGNC IDs or symbols, building a list of gene info, and storing it along with phenotype IDs in the case document.
Fetches a single case from the collection by ID or by institute and display name, raising an error if insufficient parameters.
Deletes a case from the collection by ID or by institute and display name, logging the action and returning the deletion result.
Adds a new case to the database, raising an IntegrityError if a case with the same ID already exists.
Replaces an existing case document in the database with the provided case object, updating its timestamp and returning the updated document.
Updates a case to a new family ID by copying the case, updating all variant and ACMG references, updating related events, inserting the new case, and deleting the old one.

Submits an evaluation for a variant by extracting IDs, determining its ACMG classification from the given criteria, building and loading the evaluation record, updating the variant’s classification, and returning the classification.
Retrieves all evaluations for a given variant from the ACMG collection, sorted by most recent creation date.
Parses transcript data (from a DataFrame or list), aggregating each transcript’s chromosome, start/end, gene ID, and RefSeq mRNA/ncRNA identifiers into a dictionary keyed by transcript ID.

Computes average ON and OFF spectra by folding the data over diode switching periods, optionally swapping the ON/OFF order and returning the index ranges.
